notes.meaning: Solomon calls his student to listen closely to wise teaching. Bending the ear means leaning in to give full, undivided attention. This godly guidance comes from experienced teachers and shows how to avoid moral ruin.

Listening to wisdom trains a person to exercise good judgment. Discretion means thinking ahead so that you choose what is right and reject what is wrong. Guarding knowledge in your heart also helps your lips speak truth rather than falling for tempting words.

The teacher warns against the enticing speech of an immoral woman. Her words seem as sweet as honey dripping from a honeycomb and as smooth as fine oil. Temptation almost always begins with flattering talk and pleasing promises.

The pleasure promised by the adulteress quickly turns to bitter pain. Wormwood was a notoriously bitter and poisonous plant, and a double-edged sword cuts painfully in every direction. Sin may feel sweet at first, but it always ends in deep remorse and severe harm.

Following an unfaithful person leads directly toward death. Her path takes a firm hold on Sheol, the dark realm of the dead and the grave. Immorality destroys a person's life on earth and leads to eternal judgment.

The immoral woman does not think about the path that leads to life. Her ways wander constantly from one deceptive trick to another, and she does not even realize how unstable she is. She stumbles along in spiritual blindness, pulling others down with her.

The teacher pauses to plead directly with his young listeners. He addresses them as sons, showing a father's genuine concern for their safety. Stepping aside from his instructions puts a young person in grave danger.

The only safe response to sexual temptation is to stay as far away from it as possible. A person should not test their willpower by walking anywhere near her doorway. Running away from dangerous situations protects the heart before wrong desires can take over.

Giving in to lust strips a person of their strength, honor, and youthful vigor. The sinner ends up handing the best years of his life over to an unmerciful partner. Sinful companions may pretend to love, but in the end they take everything and show no pity.

Immorality rapidly destroys a person's financial security. Hard-earned wealth and the fruit of years of painful labor end up in the hands of strangers and foreigners. Yielding to lust wastes resources that should have cared for one's own family.

Toward the close of life, the ruined man groans aloud in agony like a wounded beast. His physical body is wasted away by the diseases and stress brought on by a reckless lifestyle. Sin promises excitement but leaves behind broken health and bitter regret.

The suffering sinner looks back with terrible regret at his foolish choices. He cries out about how much he hated discipline and pushed away every loving correction. The worst grief comes from knowing that one's own stubbornness caused all the pain.

The ruined man confesses that he refused to listen to parents, mentors, and teachers. He stopped his ears and dismissed the good advice that was meant to protect him. Refusing to hear wise guidance leaves a person completely defenseless against temptation.

What was done in secret ends up exposed to everyone. The offender finds himself on the brink of total ruin and open disgrace right in front of the assembled community. In ancient Israel, such open shame also brought the danger of legal trial and severe punishment.

Solomon points to lawful marriage as God's pure gift and remedy against lust. Drinking water from one's own cistern and well describes finding full sexual and emotional satisfaction in one's own spouse. God designed the marriage bond to meet deep human needs in an exclusive, holy way.

The teacher asks why a man would squander his intimate strength out in public streets. Pure springs should never be allowed to spill wastefully into dirty town squares. A man's intimate affections and family line must never be scattered among prostitutes.

The waters of marital love and family belong solely to the husband and wife. Marital intimacy is a private treasure meant to remain within the home, never shared with outsiders. Guarding this boundary keeps a marriage safe and pure.

The teacher prays a blessing over the marriage union and urges the husband to rejoice in his wife. 'The wife of your youth' points to marrying early and staying completely devoted to her throughout life. God gives real joy to couples who cultivate lifetime faithfulness.

The wife is pictured as a graceful deer, an animal known in ancient poetry for gentleness, beauty, and affection. Scripture unashamedly celebrates physical delight and romantic warmth within the safety of marriage. A husband is called to be continuously captivated by his wife's love.

Solomon asks why any man would trade the pure joy of marriage for the embrace of an adulteress. It makes no sense to chase after a forbidden stranger when God provides true delight at home. Sin tempts people to search outside God's boundaries for what He already offers within them.

People may hide their secret sins from other human beings, but nothing is hidden from the Lord. God watches every single step a person takes and carefully weighs every action. Remembering that the Lord sees everything helps guard the heart against secret sin.

The wicked man is caught in a trap of his own making. Repeated sinful choices turn into heavy cords that bind him fast until he cannot break free. Sin always promises freedom, but it ends in total slavery.

The sinner perishes because he refuses to exercise self-control and rejects God's instruction. His own stubborn foolishness leads him off the path of life and into destruction. Disregarding godly correction brings a person to sudden and permanent ruin.
